html:
The Mojeños, or Moxos, are an Arawakan people of the Llanos de Mojos, the seasonally flooded plains of the Mamoré River in Bolivia's Beni department. Long before 1492, people in this region raised their fields above the floods and built canals, fish weirs, causeways and mounds.

From 1682 Jesuit missionaries gathered the Mojeños into mission towns such as Loreto and Trinidad, run much like the reductions of Paraguay. They became skilled musicians, carvers and weavers. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, the missions declined under Spanish officials. In the rubber boom around 1900 many Mojeños were taken away as labourers. Their neighbours include the Baure, Movima and Canichana.
